# Phase Two — Gevurah Critique

The Awtsmoos is beyond every codec, yet Awtsmoos.com needs boundaries so evidence cannot be mistaken for hope.

1. Do not modify the worker encoder if its existing frameSource contract already suffices.
2. Do not install Playwright/Puppeteer/Canvas; native tunnel Chrome control is already available.
3. Do not invent media verification from metadata; require ffprobe.
4. Do not use one repeated frame; require sampled witnesses at distant timestamps.
5. Do not overwrite the existing festival export page; create a canonical proof page beside it.
6. Do not rewrite `AnimatorMovieExportEngine.js` unless call tracing proves it is required; it is already modified by other work.
7. Do not add dialogue until browser voice scheduling is inspected and known cast IDs can be handled safely.
8. Keep canonical frame source independent from app state and global DOM selectors.
9. Validate the movie before export and fail with exact structured validation messages.
10. Frame source `capture()` must translate milliseconds to canonical seconds exactly once.
11. `prepare()` must set canvas dimensions explicitly and avoid CSS-only sizing assumptions.
12. Every captured `ImageBitmap` must come from the rendered canonical canvas, not a stale preview.
13. Keep export modules below 120 lines; split page, frame source, bridge, and persistence responsibilities.
14. Tests are written only after source first draft is complete, per repository constitution.
15. Browser automation must inspect console errors and final global state, not just page load.
16. Final proof file needs a deterministic path that shell tools can inspect.
17. If browser download interception is unreliable, add a tiny local receiver only if the existing tunnel/browser cannot expose the Blob; do not fake success.
18. Final completion requires reread, delta, hidden-work search, and updated evidence ledger.
